subject: POC orchestration: hands-on session — room vs virtual?
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@stratoretail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: ops@stratoretail.com
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC hands-on session — next steps and logistics

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the execs were impressed and want to move to a hands-on POC. We’re targeting a 1-day working session focused on prompt review/routing, a short load test, and running through the prefix caching flow with our sample catalog. High-level asks:

- Prefer onsite at our HQ (San Jose) but open to hybrid if you recommend it.
- Attendees: ~10 Strato engineers + 4 product folks.
- We need screen share, room A/V, and permission to record for internal training.
- Can you confirm engineer availability and any hardware requirements?

Proposed windows (all PT):
- Tue 2027-05-18 (9:30–17:00)
- Thu 2027-05-20 (10:00–16:00)

If those don’t work, we can slide into the week of May 24. Also attaching our floorplan for access/security considerations (ops@ copied).

Appreciate a quick confirmation so I can block rooms on our side.

Cheers,
Evan Torres
Director, Platform Eng — Strato Retail
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@stratoretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session — next steps and logistics

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and floorplan. We can absolutely run the hands-on session you describe. A few quick clarifying items before we lock dates: 

1) Core Redwood team we’d plan to bring: myself (PM lead), Ben (Solutions Engineer), Marcus (inference engineer) — Marcus will own the load test and kernel/quantization discussion.
2) For an onsite session we’ll need a private room with HDMI + Mac laptop adapter and a table for a small bench (we’ll bring one). Can your security team pre-approve guest badges and a white-list of laptop MACs if your network policy requires it?
3) Recording: we typically record sessions when customers permit; we’ll want a short recording consent note in the runbook and will isolate any PII from logs.

Availability on our side: Marcus is out May 18, but we can do May 20 (10:00–16:00) or move to the week of May 24 — Ben, can you confirm which of the proposed windows you can cover if Marcus is not available?

We’ve attached a preliminary runbook and a visitor template that your ops team can fill out (we’ll need names + company ID + expected arrival times). Also, if you want a hybrid fallback we can stream via Zoom and keep one engineer remote.

Attached: redwood-prelim-runbook.pdf

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Evan Torres <evan.torres@stratoretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session — next steps and logistics

Kimberly / Evan — quick note: Marcus is available May 20 and the week of May 24; he’s out on May 18 as Kimberly mentioned. If May 20 works for Strato, I’ll prep the load test script (target ~100 concurrent prompt threads, 4s p99 goal) and bring a small test harness.

Also to be transparent on capacity: if you want simultaneous heavy routing (multiple model variants) we should plan a short warm-up run in the morning and a 30m high-throughput validation after lunch.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@stratoretail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@stratoretail.com
Date: 2027-05-14T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC hands-on session — next steps and logistics

Thanks Ben/Kimberly — May 20 looks better for us now, but one ask: our VP of Ops is traveling and only available the morning. Is it possible to compress the agenda to 9:30–15:30 and still get the essential load test + routing review? Also:

- We’d prefer onsite but can do hybrid if that makes it easier for your engineers.
- We need the visitor_template.csv you referenced — attaching our current guest-policy checklist and our updated floorplan (strato-floorplan-v2.pdf).
- Recording: Ops prefers a short pre-recording consent email to attendees and that the recording is stored in our shared GDrive.

Can you send the visitor template and confirm the compressed timeline works?

Thanks,
Evan
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@stratoretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-16T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC orchestration: hands-on session — room vs virtual?

Evan — confirmed: May 20, 2027, 09:30–15:30 PT, onsite at Strato HQ (Room B, nearest to reception). We’ll compress the agenda to hit the essentials:

Agenda (compressed):
- 09:30–10:00 Intro + goals / consent to record
- 10:00–11:30 Prompt review & routing decisions (prompt sets + model variants)
- 11:30–12:00 Short warm-up & lunch break
- 12:00–13:30 Load test (target: 100 concurrent threads; warm-up + 30m high-throughput validation)
- 13:30–14:30 KV/prefix caching walkthrough + immediate tuning recommendations
- 14:30–15:00 Runbook & next steps / handoff

Logistics & attachments: 
- Visitor template attached: visitor_template.csv (please return with final names, company ID, and arrival times by EOD 2027-05-18).
- We’ll bring a MacBook + HDMI adapter; Marcus will bring the harness.
- Recording: we will record and upload to your Drive link — please confirm Ops is comfortable and we’ll add the short consent item at the top of the agenda.
- Room booking: https://booking.redwood.com/rooms/42 (we’ve tentatively reserved a Redwood engineer desk at your location).

Please confirm final headcount and dietary restrictions for the lunch order. If anything changes on your side we can pivot to hybrid; otherwise we’ll plan to be onsite.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
redwood.com | kimberly_park@redwood.com
